items.title: European-made pesticides named in 1,605 poisoning reports in Brazil last year
paragraphs: Pesticides sold by European chemical companies were named in more than 1,600 poisoning reports in Brazil last year, an investigation has found.

About a third of the cases involved chemicals banned from use on farms in the EU because of the risks they pose to people and the environment. But European companies are not banned from manufacturing these chemicals, as long as they export them overseas to countries where they are legally allowed to be used.

Analysis of Brazilian health ministry data by Unearthed and Public Eye in a report published on Tuesday found that of 2,857 poisoning reports that named an identifiable agricultural product, 1,605 named brands sold by European pesticide companies.

Farm workers in Brazil have described their flesh rotting, skin burning, difficulty breathing and vomiting after using the chemicals at work, according to the report. A small number have died accidentally or killed themselves by drinking the pesticides.

Under Brazilian law, reports must be submitted by healthcare professionals to Brazil’s national disease notification system in all suspected pesticide poisoning cases. These reports can be marked “confirmed” poisoning or “exposure” only by the doctor or nurse who saw the patient.

Clinicians sometimes record cases as exposure when they lack the training or support to confirm a diagnosis, but are presented with a patient who says they have been exposed to pesticides or present symptoms of pesticide poisoning. Laboratory confirmation is rare, so recording a diagnosis of “confirmed” poisoning usually depends on clinical judgment.
Experts say clinicians can be reluctant to confirm cases because of a lack of training or support. A brand being named in a poisoning report is not proof that it caused poisoning or death.

“The insufficient training of healthcare professionals to recognise and manage these cases is a major limiting factor,” said Vanda Garibotti, a public health biologist at the State Centre for Health Surveillance in Rio Grande do Sul, southern Brazil.
High staff turnover and a lack of institutional support meant poisoning cases were rarely confirmed through laboratory tests and often relied on clinical judgment, Garibotti added.

In more than 6,700 medical reports involving agricultural pesticides last year, 2,857 named an identifiable product. Of those, 1,420 were classified as confirmed poisonings. A further 1,108 were classified as exposures; for the remainder the classification was unknown or other diagnoses.

Some of the products are made in Britain. Reglone is the most frequently cited UK-made weedkiller. It contains diquat, a chemical that was banned in the UK in 2020 after experts concluded it posed a high risk to people living near fields where it was sprayed. Diquat is also found in other pesticides.

Despite the usage ban, Reglone is still manufactured by the Swiss-headquartered pesticides company Syngenta at its factory in Huddersfield for export to countries with more permissive regulations, including Brazil.

Nelson Castoldi died last year after accidentally ingesting Reglone on his family farm in Rio Grande do Sul. To save money, his family had bought the weedkiller in bulk, decanting a single litre into an empty cola bottle to avoid hauling a heavy 20-litre canister into the fields.

Working under the scorching sun, Castoldi mistook the black chemical for a soft drink and took a sip. Though he spat it out immediately, the chemical caused his kidneys to fail before attacking his lungs. He died two days later.

“We fell apart,” Ivan Castoldi said of his father’s death. “Four months after our father passed away, our mother also passed away. She cried day and night. She became depressive and had a stroke. She was left alone.
“That poison, Reglone, should be banned in Brazil,” he added. “Not because of what happened to us, but because of its toxicity.”
The Brazilian health ministry recorded 75 cases involving diquat last year, compared with 36 over the five years from 2018 to 2022.

The investigation found Reglone was specifically named in 44 reports, including four deaths. Of those cases, 26 were classified as confirmed poisonings and the rest were classified as exposure, unknown, or adverse reaction.
Dormex, a pesticide manufactured in Germany by Alzchem and distributed in Brazil by the German chemical company BASF, is another product workers said injured them or made them ill.

Sidnei Souza de Oliveira, 49, suffered a severe injury after a jug of Dormex spilled on his leg while he was filling a sprayer. The handle broke as he was transferring the chemical into the tank. At first, his leg turned red, and he continued spraying.

He carried on working for four days before going to hospital. “After 15 days, my leg was black. Chunks of flesh were falling off,” Oliveira said. A doctor said the injury was serious and had to remove dead tissue to stop it spreading towards the bone.

Oliveira said the protective trousers supplied by his employer were thin and allowed the chemical to seep through. He said he had been afraid of losing his job if he stayed away from work for too long.

Dormex contains cyanamide, which was banned from use in the EU in 2008 because of concerns about its effects on human health, particularly among farm workers spraying the chemical. Analysis shows the Brazilian health ministry database recorded 17 confirmed poisonings involving Dormex last year.

Finale, a BASF product identified in the investigation, contains glufosinate, which was banned in the EU in 2018. Roundup – a glyphosate-based weedkiller manufactured by the German chemical company Bayer – was frequently cited in Brazilian poisoning reports, including 12 deaths.

Across all the poisoning reports identified by the investigation as involving products sold by European companies, there were 32 reported deaths. Of these cases, 31 were classified as confirmed poisonings, and 26 were recorded as suicides.

Syngenta products were cited 425 times in the poisoning reports, and BASF 179 times. The company figures are not mutually exclusive: some poisoning reports named products sold by more than one manufacturer.
Nina Schrank, a senior campaigner at Greenpeace UK, said the findings were a “deadly double standard”.

“If a pesticide is too dangerous to use in Britain, it should be too dangerous to export. Ministers must stop allowing Britain to be part of a production line for toxic chemicals that are putting lives at risk overseas.”

The EU’s pesticide approval system requires chemicals to meet strict standards for human and animal health and the environment. Diquat has been banned on EU and UK farms since 2019 and 2020 respectively, after experts concluded it posed a high risk to workers, people living nearby and birds. Cyanamide was withdrawn after an assessment found exposure among agricultural operators could exceed safe levels. Glufosinate, meanwhile, is classified in the EU as toxic to reproduction, meaning it can harm fertility or the development of unborn children.

Suicide prevention is also a factor. A 2020 study found national bans on highly hazardous pesticides could be a cost-effective intervention for reducing the number of people who kill themselves in countries with a high burden of suicides attributable to pesticides.

A Syngenta spokesperson said almost half the Brazilian cases attributed to the company were not classified as confirmed poisonings, adding: “Public Eye and Unearthed are aware of this but have explicitly chosen to disregard the dataset’s final classification.” The company accused the investigation of disregarding the dataset’s final classifications and identified “numerous other inconsistencies” that it said raised “serious concerns” that the evidence was “being selectively interpreted to support a predetermined conclusion”.
“There are real people behind these statistics. Every genuine case of poisoning matters, and every family affected deserves our concern,” the spokesperson added.

Syngenta said Brazil had its own “robust regulatory system” and that products banned in Europe could still be independently assessed and legally registered in the country, citing differences in crops, growing conditions and pest pressures. It said it trained 95,000 people in Brazil in the safe use of its products in 2025, including through free online courses.

Bayer said its products were safe when used according to label instructions, citing what it described as rigorous testing and assessments by global health authorities. The company said it took pesticide poisoning seriously but questioned the reliability of the data, arguing that products and circumstances of exposure had not been independently verified, some chemicals may have been incorrectly identified and symptoms such as headaches and skin irritation could have other causes.
It said “Roundup” was “widely used as a generic term” that could refer to weedkillers made by other manufacturers or counterfeit products.

The company said it provided training on the safe handling and use of pesticides, including protective equipment, and that its programmes reached more than 4 million people globally in 2025. It also argued that a pesticide being banned in the EU did not necessarily mean it was unsafe, saying other countries had robust regulatory systems that took account of local agricultural conditions.

It added: “While the data presented helps to provide information on broad trends of exposure, the data has limitations and warrants caution when drawing conclusions, particularly when looking at individual cases.”
BASF said it was deeply concerned by reports of poisoning that might be linked to its products, adding that it took all such incidents seriously.

A spokesperson said publicly available information suggested some incidents might have involved the intentional ingestion of crop protection products, describing such acts as “deliberate misuse” of products intended exclusively for agricultural use.

BASF said it had global and local procedures to assess and investigate incidents potentially involving its products, and worked with authorities and experts where appropriate to understand cases and identify ways to prevent similar incidents. It said it invested in education and training to promote the safe handling and use of its products, with initiatives in Brazil reaching more than 14,475 participants in 2025.
The company said it was confident in the safety of its products when used in accordance with label instructions and applicable regulatory standards.

It added that Brazilian law required crop protection products to be handled and applied only by authorised and properly trained individuals, and said it took its responsibility for ensuring their safe use seriously.

items.title: Isern Serra designs bold colour-blocked interiors for Barcelona pilates studio
paragraphs: Spanish design practice Isern Serra combined organic architectural forms with a vibrant colour palette for Circl, a fitness studio and matcha cafe located in Barcelona’s historic Eixample district.

Set just below street level, the 180-square-metre space was designed to offer an escape from the busy city centre and contains an entrance cafe, reception area, changing rooms, bathrooms and a pilates studio.
“The project began with the idea of bringing together two worlds: pilates and matcha,” Isern Serra told Dezeen.
“Although different in nature, both share a common philosophy centred on wellbeing, balance and the connection between body and mind,” he continued.
“Architecture plays an essential role in this experience, accompanying visitors on a gradual transition from the energy of the city towards a more intimate and introspective environment.”

His studio introduced a series of colour-blocked spaces to guide customers through different phases of the interior, with colours that were specifically chosen to correspond to the function and tone of each area.

“This vision of wellbeing takes shape through a carefully choreographed sequence of spaces, where each change in level, colour and atmosphere guides users away from the bustle of the city and towards an increasingly introspective environment,” said Serra.

Serra combined cream banquette seating with dark wooden tables and alabaster sconces to create a calm, meditative environment for the cafe part of the space. A sculptural, mirrored service counter was also incorporated to reflect natural light around the space.
To signal the transition into the pilates studio, the designers introduced a deep-green reception hallway with tiered seating blocks and a spherical light installation.
The bright green circulation area is connected by an open archway and features curved architectural volumes that house the changing rooms, bathrooms and a water fountain.
Another rounded archway then leads to the main studio.
The main pilates studio was designed as a white space to reflect the coloured light from a sculptural LED light installation attached to the vaulted ceiling.
The aim was to create diverse exercise environments and enable the lighting to control the mood and energy of the space.
“The white surfaces act as a neutral canvas for coloured light, allowing different hues to transform the atmosphere,” Serra said.
“This system also offers flexibility for brand collaborations, as the lighting can be adapted to reflect different identities and experiences,” he added.
In the studio, the designers used mirrored walls to create the illusion of a circular room and added full-length perimeter curtains to soften the space’s texture.
Other interior projects recently featured on Dezeen include Matteo Thun designs for Milan’s Torre Velasca skyscraper and SABO’s design of an apartment on Manhattan’s Lower East Side.

items.title: ‘His wife was horrified’: did Edward Hopper paint his sexual problems?
paragraphs: It should have been a happy occasion. In 1950, an Edward Hopper retrospective was staged at the Whitney Museum of American Art in New York – but the artist’s wife, the painter Josephine (Jo) Nivison Hopper, was in a fury. The show’s catalogue, written by the museum’s director, had originally stated that in 1924 Edward “married the artist Josephine Nivison Hopper”, yet in the final version, the phrase “the artist” had been removed. “I’m not allowed to exist even in my husband’s biography,” Jo seethed in a private notebook that has just come to light. “And that’s all right with EH.”

Due to her own strenuous efforts, Jo not only exists, but is a vital protagonist in my new biography of Edward Hopper. Jo once contemplated writing her husband’s biography herself, having amassed such an overwhelming body of material documenting their tumultuous marriage. As Edward’s creative partner, muse, curator, producer and unofficial manager, Jo produced 35 years’ worth of daily diaries, almost 100 notebooks, reels of letters, and four ledger books documenting Edward’s works.

A self-confessed “pack-rat”, she preserved everything from their film and theatre ticket stubs to magazines, catalogues and photographs. This vast material legacy, much of it housed at the Whitney, would form the backbone of my biography, the first on Edward in 30 years and only the second ever.

I was able to draw on many unpublished notebooks and diaries (including Edward’s sole notebook on art), which reveal new and poignant details about the Hoppers’ complex relationship and artistic rivalry. In one firecracker of a notebook spanning nearly 80 pages, Jo not only reveals the alarming abuse she suffered and their unsatisfactory sex life, but also recounts the whirlwind farce of their wedding day that resulted in a mad rush from church to church after Edward, who was not baptised, was turned away by a reverend. They lost their best man along the way.

Jo ultimately decided against writing Edward’s biography, explaining: “To have to think and weigh and be explicit – this big, tall, lonely, silent man … it would need expert reporting and memory to repeat his exact words for any fairness.” Indeed, Edward gave so little away that he still presents as an enigma. This is the Edward we both see and feel in such iconic works as his haunting Nighthawks, showing four people in a diner; his disquieting Automat, in which a lone woman sits in a cafe; and his ode to modern melancholia, Hotel Room, featuring another solitary woman poised on the edge of a bed reading.

However, I decided to begin with the artist’s lesser-known works and little explored formative years. I did not expect to discover that all of Edward’s earliest oils – long claimed to be originals, some supposedly depicting his home town of Nyack in upstate New York – were in fact copies from colour reproductions of other artists’ works found in Victorian periodicals, replete with copying instructions. Of course, all aspiring artists copy, but this discovery upended the myth that Edward’s painting talent arose in an art historical vacuum, showing him engaging with the American art of his era from an early age.

It is still little-recognised that the majority of Edward’s paintings are of regional subjects, mostly in New England, rather than the cityscapes he is best known for. And of all his subjects, it was a lighthouse in the remote Maine village of Two Lights that he painted the most. I wanted to know why.

The Hoppers drove to Two Lights in the summer of 1927. “We fell in love with the lighthouse,” Jo wrote, but when she attempted “a harmless little watercolour”, Edward huffed, saying: “If you’re going to paint it – I won’t.” Jo was left to sulk on the rocks, where she wrote a list of “blessings of attributes of E to be remembered in times of stress”. Sadly, that list did little to redeem Jo’s often damning opinion of her husband, whom she called a “sadist” and a “prize hog”.

Jo makes clear that Edward’s possessiveness derived from a profound identification with the lighthouse. At 6ft 4in tall, he repeatedly inferred that the awkward, tall architectures in his paintings were anthropomorphic self-portraits. In 1946, Jo wrote: “Those lighthouses are self-portraits.” She added: “That ego is impenetrable … It was pitiful to see all the poor dead birds that had run into [the lighthouses] on a dark night. I know just how they felt. That bright light on the top had deceived them.”

But for Edward, works such as 1929’s The Lighthouse at Two Lights was as close to celebratory as his art ever came. Cherishing the literature of such esteemed writers as Walt Whitman and Ralph Waldo Emerson, who embodied a historic tradition of heroic American solitude, Edward envisaged the lighthouse as a beacon of American individualism, the philosophy that he most ardently observed.

The political ramifications of his lighthouse did not stop there. In seeking to paint and thereby aggrandise New England’s regional icons, Edward, among others, sated the appetite of a fiercely nationalist and isolationist press that hungered for representations of the regional “American scene”. New England’s white Anglo-Saxon lineage and its colonial beginnings were also crucial aspects of its appeal. Edward’s work would be repeatedly referred to as “Anglo-Saxon” and “Puritan” for decades as a means of stressing his quintessential Americanness. In both his art and letters of the period, Edward capitalised on these currents, even telling one critic: “You did a swell job on me as a Puritan.”

Captain Ed Staples, a fictionalised self-portrait showing the artist as a New England sea captain in 1928, embodies these ideas. Combing through ancestral records, I discovered that the Staples surname belonged to the historic lighthouse family that had co-founded Two Lights, and that the Hopper and Staples families became firm friends. In creating this New England alter ego, Edward surely knew what he was doing. Capt Ed Staples, sadly destroyed in a 1929 train crash, was the “all-American” Edward Hopper incarnate.

As Edward’s fortunes ascended in the late 1920s, Jo’s dwindled. She had previously enjoyed artistic success in modernist circles and, in 1923, it was she who had encouraged Edward to paint in watercolours, which led to a landmark sale and the securing of Edward’s lifetime gallerist. But Edward almost never sought to help Jo with her career, and she never forgave him his neglect, nor his dismissal of female artists in general. To him, she wrote, “they were nil – zero minus etc”. Jo’s diaries consistently document Edward’s denigration of her art as well as instances of domestic abuse – albeit with flashes of lightness and humour – painting a picture of a troubled marriage and a deeply repressed man.

While they never betray the violent altercations that shocked readers when extracts from Jo’s diaries were first published in Gail Levin’s 1995 biography, Edward’s paintings, such as Four Lane Road, make the couple’s tension explicit. The female figure, confined to the interior of a gas station, leans out of the window, her mouth open, breaking the reverie of the man sitting outside, who intriguingly resembles Captain Ed Staples. Jo was horrified to see that Edward was “making the most evil face on the woman at window … a regular shrike, expressive of what he’s feeling about me”. In the painting’s ledger book entry, Jo pointedly remarked: “Woman … finds his serenity a trial.”

Elsewhere, Edward’s 1959 work Excursion into Philosophy suggests the Hoppers’ incompatible sexual relationship. It portrays a woman on a bed, turned away with her naked buttocks on display. This was surely a nod to Edward’s sexual preferences, which Jo referred to as “attacks from the rear”. Beside the woman’s buttocks is an open book that deliberately echoes their shape. Describing the painting, Jo said it was a “book of Plato … resorted to on morning after episode with young woman”. Plato clearly provides little solace for the man, who stares into a rectangle of sunlight, grappling with what seems to be his shame in the harsh light of day.

Jo modelled for Edward’s 1941 painting Girlie Show, featuring a nude burlesque performer. She could not decide whether the woman was an autonomous performer or an object of male desire, variously naming her a “minx”, “vixen” and “siren.” Ultimately, Jo reflected that she was “not as heroic” as the “big strong creature that parades so triumphantly”. On a stray scrap of paper that I found, Jo scathingly documented her experience as a model: “One doesn’t exist at all in any personal sense. He isn’t painting you. He raves about the wall … Little does he care how you freeze … with scarcely a stitch on of a cold night to see how light falls on your shivering flesh.”

Edward’s final oil painting, 1966’s Two Comedians, chose at last to acknowledge Jo as an equal partner. It shows Edward and Jo donning ruffs as a smiling Pierrot and Pierrette on a stage, holding hands and bowing out after a life together – with a nod to their favourite film Les Enfants du Paradis, the swooningly romantic 1945 tribute to theatre. “This marriage has been the one great enterprise – my kingdom come,” Jo wrote in 1939. “Our Kingdom … Of all the profoundest gifts of God: fidelity, wisely or not.”

items.title: Rio Tinto agrees to pay US$250m to begin repairing ‘devastation’ left by Panguna mine
paragraphs: Anglo-Australian miner Rio Tinto has agreed to pay a quarter-of-a-billion dollars to begin the clean-up of the toxic Panguna mine site it abandoned more than three decades ago.

Panguna, once one of the world’s most profitable gold and copper mines, was shuttered in 1989 after violent protests over environmental damage and the inequitable division of the mine’s profits sparked a decade-long civil war on the Papua New Guinean island of Bougainville.
But the sprawling mine pit, once a mountain, remains a scar in the middle of the island, with vast pillars of rubble at risk of collapse, and polluted rivers running bright blue with toxins.

Rio Tinto was forced from the island and has never returned, but in recent years has been part of a detailed consultation process with landowners and government. It has now agreed to voluntarily contribute US$250m (A$370m) towards the remediation of the mine site.

Theonila Roka Matbob, a former cabinet minister in Bougainville’s autonomous government and Panguna community leader, said the fund was a vital contribution towards repairing the “devastation left by the Panguna mine”.

“We have a lot of work still ahead of us, but the establishment of this fund gives us the chance to find solutions to the huge problems we have been living with since the days of the mine’s operation.

“No amount of money will restore the damage caused to the environment in Panguna, but this sets a foundation for us to invest in addressing the environmental issues and invest in our children’s futures as well.”

Roka Matbob said the most fundamental remediation was to improve “accessibility” for the people living around Panguna – “accessibility to clean drinking water that is safe and secure … and infrastructure, in bridges that makes people’s access to trade, to school, to health[care], much easier. This is one critical area that immediately needs attention.”

The president of Bougainville, Ishmael Toroama, seeking to become the world’s newest head of state at the forefront of a long-running independence movement on the island, said the money would make a “meaningful difference” to villages and communities that had suffered from the impacts of the mine’s pollution.

“This work will deliver benefits not only for people today, but for future generations. Continued engagement with our communities will be essential to ensuring the work responds to local priorities and delivers lasting outcomes.”

The Rio commitment has emerged from the Panguna Mine Legacy Impact Assessment consultation process, which was initiated in response to a human rights complaint brought by the Australian-based Human Rights Law Centre, with Roka Matbob as the lead complainant.
Keren Adams, the HRLC’s legal director, said establishing the fund had taken years of work.
“It is a testament to the courage and persistence of community leaders, and the willingness of all parties to engage in difficult but constructive dialogue,” she said.
“The significant funding contributed by Rio Tinto creates a real opportunity to now address an environmental disaster that has remained unresolved for decades.”

Mark Davies, Rio Tinto’s chief safety and technical officer, said the establishment of the fund was an “important milestone … intended to support the transition from the assessment to practical remedy implementation”.
“Community engagement is an important next step to identify priorities and we remain committed to working with communities to shape the activities supported by the fund.”
The quarter-of-a-billion dollars will not be sufficient to entirely remediate the mine site, but it is being seen as a major step towards rehabilitation.
The funding commitment for Panguna comes at an acutely sensitive time for the restive Bougainville island.

The mine has become inextricably linked with the Bougainville’s political future: restarting operations at Panguna – believed to still hold at least $60bn in unrealised reserves – is seen by many, including the president, as the fundamental financial basis for the island’s independent future. Indian miner Lloyds has been granted a 25-year large-scale mining lease, but any future mining is years from starting.
Bougainville, a group of islands off Papua New Guinea to the north of Australia, has been variously controlled by Britain, Germany, Japan, Australia and PNG.
It declared independence in 1975 as the Republic of North Solomons, but was absorbed into the newly independent PNG weeks later.
Its close ethnic ties and proximity to the Solomons archipelago means it has always sat uneasily with Port Moresby’s rule.
That discontent came to a violent head in 1988 after a long-running dispute over the lucrative Panguna copper and gold mine.
The mine, carved from a mountain in central Bougainville, was critically important to PNG, at one point generating more than 45% of the country's national export revenue.

Multinational Rio Tinto and other international investors earned nearly US$2bn from the mine over 17 years of operation. But less than 1% of the mine’s profits went to Bougainvilleans, whose homes and lands had been destroyed by it.
Under the leadership of a former mine worker, Francis Ona, disaffected Bougainvilleans ran a sabotage campaign which forced the mine’s closure in 1989.

The PNG Government responded by sending in police, then soldiers, to restore law and order. Bougainville was blockaded and the island descended into a brutal civil war that ran for a decade, and saw as many as 20,000 people die.
PNG later hired international mercenaries to end the conflict (the notorious Sandline affair), before a peace agreement was signed in 2001.
In a 2019 referendum, 97.7% of Bougainvilleans voted in favour of independence. Many argue that reopening Panguna mine will be key to the island’s economic future as an independent nation.

Rio Tinto and other international investors earned nearly $2bn from Panguna over 17 years of operation from 1972. But less than 1% of the mine’s profits went to Bougainvilleans, whose homes and lands were destroyed by it.

Disaffected landowners ran a sabotage campaign that forced Panguna’s closure in 1989. The PNG government responded by sending in police, then soldiers, to restore law and order. Bougainville was blockaded and the island descended into a brutal civil war – known as “the crisis” – that ran for a decade. Between 15,000 and 20,000 people were killed, roughly 10% of the island’s population.

A recent environmental impact assessment found the abandoned mine remains an acute threat to people’s lives, including from landslides, levee collapses and floods. Untouched, the river delta will stay polluted for a century.

The future of Bougainville’s independence campaign is now before the PNG parliament, which will decide whether or not to recognise a UN-backed independence referendum held on the island in 2019, in which 97.7% of voters were in favour of Bougainville seceding and becoming an independent country.
The PNG parliament, which heard lengthy and impassioned debate over Bougainville last month, appears almost certain to vote against recognising the referendum result.

But Toroama, who has staked his presidency on achieving political independence, has said, regardless of the parliament’s decision, Bougainville will enter a period of “self-government” from September next year, before seceding, breaking away from PNG as a fully fledged independent nation, by 2030.

items.title: New Zealand tricks and annual leave - the lengths fans are going to for GTA 6
paragraphs: Gamers have long been known to book time off work for major releases.

When Red Dead Redemption 2 launched in October 2018, social media users were sharing plans to take the day off, with one analytics firm reportedly finding, external more people talking about calling in sick for it than any other game that year.
Similar conversations took place ahead of Cyberpunk 2077's release in December 2020, with fans discussing , externaltaking several days off to play.
GTA 6 is no exception, but it appears to characteristically be taking things to a whole new level.
For the game's launch day, HR software company BrightHR, external looked at absence data from more than 1.2 million employees from 70,000 businesses across the UK.
It found GTA was mentioned in 4.6% of time-off requests by employees. Throughout November and December, it said an estimated 83,000 days had been booked off for the game.

According to the HR firm, one person put "new GTA is coming out! I will be spending a week on the sofa in my pants!" as the reason for their leave request, while another said: "play the new GTA - I've waited a billion years".
A third said in their request: "GTA Release - I'll put my notice in if this is denied."
The company added it had no way of tracking if the requests had actually been approved by employers.
Aside from taking time off, some gamers have also been discussing a technical loophole which could give them valuable extra hours of play before it officially unlocks in their country.

Because GTA 6 will release at midnight local time in all regions, New Zealand will become one of the first places where it is available, due to it reaching midnight earliest because of its position near the international date line.
This has led to some investigating ways to "trick" their consoles into thinking they're based in the island country when they are in fact thousands of miles away.
According to Google Trends, searches for the "GTA 6 New Zealand trick" have surged by more than 5,000% in the UK over the past month.
Games journalist Vic Hood said many gamers would be looking to play earlier to "get in on the action as soon as possible", as well as to prevent spoilers.
"As New Zealand is 13 hours ahead of the UK, that's 13 hours of gameplay that has time to spread across the internet and potentially spoil some key story beats and in-game surprises," she said.
"Took an extra day of paid time off when I found this out," one fan posted on Reddit on the trick.
It also means gamers would be playing the game at the much nicer time of 11:00 GMT, rather than having to stay up all night.

But another Xbox user shared caution on Reddit, noting that while the loophole had been exploited for many years for other game releases, GTA 6 "might be the game where Microsoft finally does something about this 'exploit'" - which could include banning players.
GTA 6's developers Rockstar and publishers Take Two Interactive have not commented on the loophole, and neither has Sony nor Microsoft.

Louise Wooldridge from analyst firm Ampere Analysis said both Microsoft and Sony had "rules governing regional accounts and purchases" for the Xbox and PlayStation, adding that Sony's were "slightly more restrictive".
Players who choose to use the workaround could therefore risk breaching those terms and conditions and potentially face restrictions on their accounts or lose access to their digital games.
Some gamers will have to wait even longer than their console-playing counterparts to get their hands on GTA 6, as the game will not be available on PC at launch, similar to previous GTA releases.
"Spare a thought for the PC users who will have to live vicariously through others' YouTube videos and Twitch streams," gamer Stephen Finn told the BBC.
A PS5 now costs from £520, while the more powerful PS5 Pro is nearly £790.
Despite the hefty price tag, for some the temptation to join the community in playing what many have called the biggest game launch of the year, if not decade, has been too great.
Reddit posts and videos, such as one by US YouTuber isoish, external, show fans buying consoles specifically to play the game.
"So, the only game I'm going to have on here is GTA," the content creator said in the video.
After more than a decade of waiting, it seems some fans are determined not to waste a single minute of GTA 6's release - no matter what the cost or extra effort.

items.title: Iranian Kurdish opposition groups reject amnesty-for-surrender deal
paragraphs: Editor's note: this story was translated from the original VOA Kurdish article.

Iranian Kurdish opposition leaders based in Iraq’s Kurdistan Region have ruled out turning themselves in to Tehran as part of potential amnesty deal, citing lack of trust in Iran to guarantee their safety.

Their comments come after Iraqi officials reported progress in negotiations involving Baghdad, the Kurdistan Regional Government (KRG) and Iran over the future of Iranian Kurdish opposition groups that have a maintained presence in northern Iraq for decades.

Iraq's Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein confirmed last week that one of the options discussed during the trilateral talks included potential amnesty for the Iranian Kurdish armed group members who wished to return, if they felt safe.

Amanj Zibaee, a member of the central committee of the Kurdistan Democratic Party of Iran (KDPI), an armed opposition group seeking greater autonomy for Kurds in Iran, and the party’s representative in Erbil, told VOA that his group categorically rejects the prospect of surrendering to Iranian authorities.
“The Islamic Republic of Iran makes many promises but offers nothing in practice. Surrendering to it is something we completely reject, and it is not even an option we have discussed,” he said.
Zibaee said his party would wait for an official announcement over the proposal discussed between Baghdad, Tehran and Erbil before determining its response.
“Once the Iraqi government and the Kurdistan Regional Government officially announce their positions, the KDPI leader will make an appropriate decision,” he said.
He said his organization has acted responsibly and has not used Iraqi territory to attack Iran, a key demand by Baghdad.
“We have never used the Kurdistan Region of Iraq as a base to launch attacks against a neighboring country. We have acted responsibly, and we will continue to do so,” Zibaee said.
Khalil Nadri, spokesperson for the Kurdistan Freedom Party, also dismissed the possibility of accepting an Iranian amnesty.

“We have an agreement with the Kurdistan Region that we will not conduct military operations against Iran from its territory. Our struggle against Iran takes place inside Iran, in Eastern Kurdistan,” Nadri told VOA, referring to predominantly Kurdish areas of western Iran.
He said his party had respected Iraqi sovereignty and helped defend the region against the Islamic State and Iran-backed armed groups, including the Popular Mobilization Forces.
“Iran is not in a position to grant us amnesty,” Nadri said. “Our homeland has been occupied. We will return when our homeland is liberated and the enemy has withdrawn.”

Iran has repeatedly over many years launched missile, and drone strikes targeting Iranian Kurdish opposition groups based in northern Iraq that have been fighting for Kurdish regional autonomy or independence in Iran. The attacks surged following the outbreak of the conflict in the Middle East as Iran launched retaliatory attacks against neighboring countries.
The Iranian Kurdish armed opposition Komala party said Monday that two missiles struck the entrance to one of its bases in the Balisan Valley in Iraq's Kurdistan Region.
Idris Kolahdozi, a member of the party's Central Committee and its head of relations in Sulaimaniyah, told VOA that the attack caused no casualties or property damage.
There was no immediate independent confirmation of who carried out the attack.

Iraqi Foreign Minister Hussein said the latest round of negotiations between Iraq, Iran and the Kurdistan Regional Government that started in October in Baghdad are continuing and that several options were under consideration.
In an interview with France 24, Hussein said the parties had reached a degree of understanding about how to address the opposition groups’ presence in Iraq.
He raised a possible amnesty deal that could allow Iranian Kurdish opposition members to return to Iran, provided they received credible guarantees for their personal safety.

Earlier this month, Iraqi government spokesperson Haider Aboudi told VOA that discussions had reached an “advanced stage” and that Baghdad hoped to resolve the issue soon, though no final deal has been publicly disclosed.
Aboudi emphasized that Iraq was determined to prevent its territory from being used to attack neighboring countries.
KRG spokesperson Peshawa Hawramani similarly told VOA that the regional government would not allow its territory to be used to harm neighboring states.

The negotiations come amid continued Iranian pressure on Baghdad and Erbil to remove Iranian Kurdish opposition groups from Iraqi territory. Tehran has repeatedly accused the groups of threatening its security, allegations the opposition parties deny.
Last month, KDPI spokesperson Khalid Azizi told VOA that his party had largely complied with Iraqi requests to withdraw from areas near the Iranian border.
He said the party had engaged in discussions with Iraqi and Kurdish authorities, with United Nations involvement, over the region's security for several years.

items.title: Met Office yellow warning in place as snow could disrupt Tuesday morning travel
paragraphs: A weather front is pushing north and east across the UK bringing a spell of rain to many areas. As this rain reaches northern England it will encounter a reservoir of colder and drier air.

Some of the rain will evaporate in this drier air, which will cool the atmosphere further by a process known as evaporative cooling - the same process involved in cooling your body down when you sweat.

Eventually rain will start to turn to snow, initially over higher hills in the Pennines, moving to lower hills with time. As the precipitation moves northwards and eastwards, the snow will spread to the Cumbrian hills and into Scotland's Southern Uplands.
The snow will come down in big, wet, chunky flakes which could stick to powerlines and tree branches.
The extra weight of the snow combined with wind gusts of 40-50mph over high ground could bring down tree branches and powerlines, bringing an additional risk of some localised power cuts.

items.title: Aged 16-24 and looking for work? Use our look-up to find out which areas have the most jobs
paragraphs: ByTommy LumbyBusiness data journalist and Nick EdserBusiness reporter
If you're one of the nearly one million people aged 16-24 not in education, employment or training - otherwise known as "Neet" - then you might be wondering where to start.
Under-25s should be guaranteed job placements or training to help them find permanent work, a major review aimed at cutting the number of Neets will say.
But how many jobs are there where you live and in which sectors are you most likely to find an opening?

There is no official measure of how many vacancies are suitable for young people, but across the whole economy there were 691,000 jobs available in the July to September period this year, which is the lowest number since early 2021.
The Covid pandemic led to huge swings in the number of job vacancies available as companies reacted to shutdowns and then reopened as restrictions were lifted.
Stripping out the fluctuations seen during the pandemic, the number of vacancies is now at its lowest level for 12 years.
Apprenticeships have often been a way for people to get their first taste of employment.

In England the number of people starting apprenticeships has risen in recent years, although this has been driven by an increase in those aged 25 and over after schemes for older workers were fully rolled out in 2008.
The number of people aged 24 and under starting apprenticeships in England in 2025 was 172,230, down from a recent peak of 291,300 in 2012.
Where you live will often have a big impact on your ability to find a job.
We have used online job adverts to help identify the number of vacancies suitable for young people in the area they live, relative to the size of the local population.
The Institute for Public Policy Research (IPPR) think tank used AI to help identify the jobs, which were broadly defined as roles requiring relatively low experience or education.
According to its analysis, South Oxfordshire had 387 suitable vacancies per 1,000 18 to 24-year-olds in the area - the most of any local authority. Rotherham had the least, at 53 per 1,000.
Use this tool to check out the situation in your area. The data for London is only available for the region as a whole and is not broken down by individual councils.
Even if there are jobs available in your area, you might not find one in the sector you want to work in.

The sector with the highest average number of entry-level vacancies in the year to October was teaching, with most of those jobs being for teaching assistants, learning support and cover supervisor roles, according to jobs website Adzuna.
The next largest was hospitality and catering, traditionally an area where younger people get their first experience of work.
Adzuna, a major online jobs website, includes adverts for full-time roles marked as entry-level, those asking for up to two years' experience, graduate roles, internships and apprenticeships.
Accounting and finance had the third-highest number of job openings.
Figures on salaries for vacancies can be patchy because many employers do not include them in job adverts.
Prime Minister Andy Burnham recently urged businesses to start publishing salaries ahead of plans to make pay details compulsory in adverts.
Only about 40% of Adzuna's jobs data for the year to October stated a salary, although that figure varies widely by sector.

Here are the average salaries for jobs in the sectors with the largest number of entry-level jobs, according to Adzuna. The highest average salary is £30,530 in engineering, while social care has the lowest at £25,880.
